# Completing and Removing Tasks

#### Course: JavaScript in Browser

## Completing and Removing Tasks

Let's add the functionalities for completing and removing tasks.

```html
1<div id="container">
2    <h1 id="title">To-do List</h1>
3    <button id="add-list-btn">List Item</button>
4    <div id="todo-lists"></div>
5</div>
6<button id="clear-all-btn">Clear All</button>
```

```css
1.completed {
2    text-decoration: line-through;
3}
```

```javascript
1addListBtn.addEventListener("click", () => {
2    ...
3
4    // Add the class completed when checkbox is checked.
5    checkbox.addEventListener("change", () => {
6        inputField.classList.toggle("completed");
7    });
8
9    // Set new placeholder value using user's value.
10    inputField.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
11        if (e.key === "Enter") {
12            inputField.setAttribute("readonly", true);
13            inputField.blur();
14        }
15    });
16
17    // Delete list when delete button is clicked.
18    deleteBtn.addEventListener("click", () => {
19        todoListsContainer.removeChild(todoItem);
20    });
21
22    todoItem.append(checkbox, inputField, deleteBtn);
23
24    todoListsContainer.appendChild(todoItem);
25});
```

Run the above code, click the "+ List Item" button, and fill in the text field.

Notice how clicking the checkbox crosses out the task, marking it as complete. Clicking the delete (X) button removes the task from the list.

However, the to-do list currently allows adding new tasks without checking if the existing text fields are empty.

Let's fix that on the next page.
